title_en: Mo Zhihua and Shenzhen Dongshen Engineering Co., Ltd. v. Dongguan Changfu Plaza Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over construction project contract
ruling_gist_en: Given the special nature of construction projects, although the contract is invalid, the labor and construction materials of the builder have been incorporated into the construction project. Pursuant to Article 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Construction Project Construction Contracts, if a construction project contract is invalid but the project has passed inspection upon completion, and the contractor requests to be treated by reference to a valid contract, the contract price shall be calculated by reference to the contract terms, and the contractor should not receive more benefits than it would have if the contract were valid.

full_text_en:
Mo Zhihua and Shenzhen Dongshen Engineering Co., Ltd. v.

Dongguan Changfu Plaza Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.

— dispute over construction project contract

[Ruling Summary]

In view of the special nature of construction projects, although the contract is invalid, the labor and construction materials of the builder have been incorporated into the construction project. According to Article 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Construction Project Contracts, if the construction project contract is invalid but the construction project has passed completion acceptance, and the contractor requests to be treated with reference to a valid contract, the contract price for the project involved shall be calculated with reference to the contract, and the contractor shall not obtain more benefits than if the contract were valid.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2011) Min Ti Zi No. 235

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Counterclaim Defendant, Appellant at Second Instance): Mo Zhihua, male, Han ethnicity, born on August 14, 1956, residing at No. 6 Xizha Street, Taiping Neighborhood Committee, Taiping Town, Qingxin County, Guangdong Province.

Agent ad litem: Zhu Haibo, lawyer at Guangdong Zhiyang Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wei Ning, lawyer at Beijing Kaiyue Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Counterclaim Plaintiff, Appellee at Second Instance): Dongguan Changfu Plaza Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 238 Changfu Commercial Pedestrian Street, Dalang Town, Dongguan City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Ye Jianyang, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Agent ad litem: He Zhengjun, lawyer at Guangdong San'en Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Lan Hua, lawyer at Guangdong San'en Law Firm.

Plaintiff at First Instance: Shenzhen Dongshen Engineering Co., Ltd., domiciled at First Floor, Office Building of Dongjiang-Shenzhen Water Supply Project Administration Bureau, South of Shuiku, Luohu District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Lin Jinyu, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Agent ad litem: Wang Zheng, employee of the company.

Agent ad litem: Zhou Na, employee of the company.

The applicant for retrial, Mo Zhihua, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2008) Yue Gao Fa Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 71 of the Guangdong High People's Court in the dispute over a construction project contract with the respondent Dongguan Changfu Plaza Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Changfu Plaza Company) and the plaintiff at first instance Shenzhen Dongshen Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dongshen Company), filed an application for retrial with this Court. This Court rendered a civil ruling (2010) Min Shen Zi No. 1418 on December 2, 2010, ordering a retrial of this case. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and heard this case in open court. Mo Zhihua and his agents ad litem Zhu Haibo and Wei Ning, the agent ad litem of Changfu Plaza Company He Zhengjun, and the agents ad litem of Dongshen Company Wang Zheng and Zhou Na appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case is now concluded.

Mo Zhihua alleged in the first instance: In early 2003, Mo Zhihua held multiple negotiations with Changfu Plaza Company to undertake the construction of the Dongguan Changfu Commercial Plaza project. After Mo Zhihua paid Changfu Plaza Company RMB 500,000 as a bid bond (subsequently converted into a performance bond), Changfu Plaza Company agreed that Mo Zhihua would undertake the project, but also required that Mo Zhihua must bid, sign contracts, and apply for construction approval in the name of a company with a Class 2 construction qualification. On April 30, 2003, Mo Zhihua and Shenzhen Dongshen Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dongshen Company) signed the Changfu Commercial Plaza Project Cooperation Agreement, establishing a contingent affiliation contracting relationship between the two parties for the Dongguan Changfu Commercial Plaza project. On May 11 of the same year, Mo Zhihua, in the name of Dongshen Company, signed the Changfu Plaza Project Preliminary Agreement with Changfu Plaza Company, stipulating that the project to be undertaken by Mo Zhihua was divided into three parts: Part 1 was the commercial-residential building and basement project with a design area of 80,523 square meters; Part 2 was the pedestrian street view and facilities; Part 3 was the electrical installation project, for which Mo Zhihua had priority contracting rights under equal conditions. Mo Zhihua and Changfu Plaza Company further signed the Dongguan Construction Project Construction Contract and the Dalang Changfu Commercial Plaza Construction Contract on May 19 and May 21 of the same year respectively. However, the project cost in the above construction contracts was roughly estimated based on preliminary design drawings and was inaccurate. Changfu Plaza Company and Mo Zhihua agreed to commence construction first, with the project cost to be settled based on the actual quantities as per the reviewed design and construction drawings. After paying a performance bond of RMB 2.7 million, Mo Zhihua commenced construction on site from June 23, 2003, to the end of 2003, investing a total of RMB 5.5 million in cash and approximately RMB 3 million worth of equipment and materials. During this period, Changfu Plaza Company did not pay any progress payments. Starting from the second half of 2003, construction material prices continuously and significantly increased, substantially raising the project cost. Although Mo Zhihua negotiated with Changfu Plaza Company multiple times regarding cost adjustments, no agreement was reached. Under these circumstances, Mo Zhihua still actively took measures to ensure normal construction. As of March 31, 2005, Mo Zhihua had completed all civil engineering works for buildings totaling 70,522 square meters (including one 3-story building, one 4-story building, one 6-story building, two 12-story buildings, and two 16-story buildings), 12,800 square meters of basement works, and other agreed-upon, additional, and modified works. Only a small portion of interior and exterior wall works below the podium of the two 12-story buildings and two 16-story buildings remained unfinished because Changfu Plaza Company stopped paying project funds. Mo Zhihua actually completed an amount of work equivalent to RMB 76,291,753.31, but Changfu Plaza Company only paid RMB 57,860,815.68 in project funds, still owing Mo Zhihua RMB 18,430,937.83 in project payments. During the cooperation between the parties, Changfu Plaza Company did not award the pedestrian street view and facilities project to Mo Zhihua, and deprived Mo Zhihua of the priority contracting right for the third part of the project, the electrical installation project; it did not increase project investment as agreed, but instead required Mo Zhihua to bear the consequences of the substantial increase in construction material prices; Changfu Plaza Company failed to timely confirm relevant project modification plans, causing serious delays in the project schedule and increasing Mo Zhihua's costs; before the project was delivered or subjected to any acceptance inspection, it forcibly put part of the building into use, which was seriously illegal and affected the project schedule. In summary, Mo Zhihua requested the court of first instance to order: 1. Changfu Plaza Company to pay Mo Zhihua project funds of RMB 18,431,937.83 and interest thereon from the filing date until the date of full payment (at the same type loan interest rate published by the People's Bank for the corresponding period); 2. Changfu Plaza Company to return the performance bond of RMB 2.7 million to Mo Zhihua and interest thereon from the date of payment to the date of return (at the same type loan interest rate published by the People's Bank for the corresponding period), calculated to March 31, 2005, as RMB 278,302.5; 3. Changfu Plaza Company to bear all litigation costs and appraisal fees of this case.

Dongshen Company alleged in the first instance: In April 2003, Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company entered into the Changfu Commercial Plaza Project Cooperation Agreement. In May 2003, Mo Zhihua, in the name of Dongshen Company, signed the Changfu Plaza Project Preliminary Agreement with Changfu Plaza Company. Now Mo Zhihua, on the ground that contingent affiliation contracting for construction projects violates relevant national laws, has filed a lawsuit with the court requesting the rescission of the contract with Changfu Plaza Company and demanding Changfu Plaza Company to pay project funds and return the performance bond and related interest. To protect its own legitimate rights and interests, Dongshen Company specially files this lawsuit, requesting the court of first instance to order: 1. Changfu Plaza Company to pay Dongshen Company project funds of RMB 18,430,937.83 and interest thereon from the filing date until the date of full payment (at the same type loan interest rate published by the People's Bank for the corresponding period), with the above amount to be paid into Dongshen Company's account; 2. Changfu Plaza Company to return the performance bond of RMB 2.7 million to Dongshen Company and interest thereon from the date of payment to the date of return (at the same type loan interest rate published by the People's Bank for the corresponding period), calculated to March 31, 2005, as RMB 278,302.5, with the above amount to be paid into Dongshen Company's account; 3. Changfu Plaza Company to bear all litigation costs of this case.

Changfu Plaza Company filed a counterclaim and defense in the first instance, alleging that the final agreed total project cost with Dongshen Company was approximately RMB 54.8 million, with the contract period from June 1, 2003, to July 31, 2004, totaling 420 days. It strictly performed its payment obligations in accordance with the agreement and actually paid project funds of RMB 57,166,406.48. However, Dongshen Company unreasonably ceased work, withdrew from the project construction prematurely, and failed to complete the project work. Dongshen Company's breach of contract has already caused substantial economic losses to Changfu Plaza Company. Changfu Plaza Company believes that Mo Zhihua may have conspired with Dongshen Company to fabricate contract documents in order to nullify the contract signed between Changfu Plaza Company and Dongshen Company, evade legal liability, and escape contractual responsibility. Therefore, it requested the court of first instance to order Dongshen Company and Mo Zhihua: 1. To return overpaid project funds of RMB 4,871,657.84; 2. To compensate Changfu Plaza Company for other economic losses of RMB 2,918,177.97, including: (1) Interest on advanced project funds of RMB 236,177.97, calculated from August 1, 2004, to June 1, 2005 (with subsequent accruals); (2) Liquidated damages for delayed project delivery of RMB 1,818,000 (calculated at RMB 6,000 per day, from August 1, 2004, to June 1, 2005); (3) Economic losses of RMB 864,000 from the attachment of property valued at RMB 15 million (from the date of attachment on August 23, 2005, until the date of release, calculated by reference to the same period bank loan rate, provisionally calculated to August 23, 2006); 3. To bear the litigation costs of this case.

Neither Mo Zhihua nor Dongshen Company submitted a defense to Changfu Plaza Company's counterclaim.

The Dongguan Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province found the following facts at first instance: On April 30, 2003, Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company entered into the Changfu Commercial Plaza Project Cooperation Agreement, under which Mo Zhihua would sign the construction contract for the Dalang Commercial Plaza project with the construction unit in the name of Dongshen Company, with Mo Zhihua actually enjoying and bearing Dongshen Company’s rights and obligations, and Mo Zhihua would pay Dongshen Company a fee of 1.5% of the project cost as Dongshen Company’s project management fee. On May 13, 2003, Dongshen Company and Changfu Plaza Company entered into the Changfu Plaza Project Preliminary Agreement. On May 19, 2003, Dongshen Company and Changfu Plaza Company signed the Dongguan Construction Project Construction Contract. On May 21, 2003, Dongshen Company and Changfu Plaza Company entered into the Dalang Changfu Commercial Plaza Construction Contract. The scope of work was: civil engineering works (excluding secondary decoration works, but including interior wall and ceiling leveling and smoothing, reservation of ceiling conduit lines), water supply and drainage works, lightning protection works (including basic lightning protection facilities and lightning protection construction for balcony railings, metal components, and aluminum windows), basement decoration works, public stairway decoration works, etc. The total construction area was 80,523 square meters. The total quantity of work was based on the construction drawings determined after comprehensive review by the parties, the design unit, and the supervision unit, with construction to be carried out according to the construction drawings. Dongshen Company's construction included not only all necessary work, management, and expenses required for the project construction, but also temporary facilities, environmental protection facilities, temporary works, and government charges on the contractor that were necessary for the project construction. The contract determined the project cost to be RMB 54.8 million, with current quotas serving only as a reference for cost calculation. Except for circumstances allowing adjustment as specified in the contract, any changes in market prices and conditions could not serve as a reason for price adjustment. For the civil works and installation works, the cost was prepared in accordance with the Guangdong Province Construction Project Budget Quota [2001 Budget Quota] (for civil works) and the Guangdong Province [2002 Budget Quota] (for installation works), with reference to the sixth issue of the Dongguan Project Cost Management Information for 2002 and current material prices in Dongguan. Civil works were charged at the standard for Class III projects, and other works were charged according to relevant regulations. The project cost, unless otherwise agreed in the contract, was subject to a 16.5% reduction. All other costs not included in the budget, such as costs for equipment and personnel mobilization and demobilization, protective net fees, sanitation fees, soil resource fees, spoil disposal fees, construction interference between adjacent contractors, etc., had been comprehensively considered by the contractor in the bid offer price reduction rate at the time of negotiation and were not to be calculated during settlement. Civilization construction fees were included in the contract price budget. Calculation rules for project cost: if there was a conflict between the contract documents and the interpretations published by the quota station, the contract documents prevailed. Contents of budget lump sum fees: removal of construction rainwater, secondary handling of materials within the site due to terrain effects, pressure measures for construction water, garbage removal after completion and site clearance, organization of construction material storage areas, labor and material costs for patching holes after water and electricity installation, protection costs for finished works, temporary water and power outages during construction, foundation collapse, daytime lighting surcharge (not including basement and special projects), site hardening, and temporary roads on the construction site. The contract stipulated that if Dongshen Company subcontracted the project to other units or individuals, Changfu Plaza Company, upon discovery, would immediately rescind the contract and forfeit the performance bond, and Dongshen Company would bear all losses incurred by Changfu Plaza Company as a result. The contract set the project duration at 420 days. If Dongshen Company failed to commence work as stipulated in the contract or failed to construct according to the approved construction plan, causing serious delays in construction progress, and after written notice from Changfu Plaza Company and the supervision engineer requiring correction, failed to take corrective measures within 14 days, Changfu Plaza Company had the right to rescind the contract and forfeit the performance bond, or readjust the scope of work under the contract, and Dongshen Company would bear all losses incurred by Changfu Plaza Company as a result. If the project schedule was delayed due to Dongshen Company's fault, a penalty of RMB 6,000 per day of delay would be imposed. In Annex 1, Dongshen Company declared: if any changes in relevant national policies, regulations, quotas, prices, or industry standards occurring during contract performance involved adjustments to the project cost, except for circumstances permitting adjustment as provided in the contract, Dongshen Company voluntarily remained bound by the terms of the contract and voluntarily waived the right to claim additional costs due to such changes. Regarding the signed Dongguan Construction Project Construction Contract, the parties agreed that it was solely for Dongshen Company to use for construction approval procedures, and all performance of contract terms was governed by the Dalang Changfu Commercial Plaza Construction Contract. After the above agreements were signed, Mo Zhihua commenced construction on June 23, 2003. Changfu Plaza Company made design changes and added some work during the process. During the construction, due to material price increases and other reasons, Mo Zhihua, Dongshen Company, and Changfu Plaza Company held multiple negotiations but failed to reach an agreement. Under the coordination of the Dongguan City Construction Bureau, Dongshen Company undertook to withdraw from the site. Due to disputes over the cost of completed work, Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company subsequently filed the lawsuit. The project cost had not been settled prior to the lawsuit. During the litigation, Mo Zhihua applied for an appraisal of the project cost. In the litigation, Mo Zhihua confirmed that Changfu Plaza Company had paid project funds totaling RMB 57,860,815.68.

The court of first instance further found that Mo Zhihua, in the name of the Qingxin County Qingxin Construction Installation Engineering Company, Dongguan Branch, remitted RMB 500,000 to Dongguan Changhe Property Investment Co., Ltd. via China Construction Bank on April 30, 2003, with the transfer slip indicating the type of instrument as project bid bond. Mo Zhihua, in the name of Dongguan Jinxinlian Industrial Investment Co., Ltd., remitted RMB 2.2 million to Changfu Plaza Company via Guangdong Development Bank, Dongguan Branch on May 23, 2003. Mo Zhihua, in the name of the Qingxin County Qingxin Construction Installation Engineering Company, Dongguan Liaison Office, remitted RMB 300,000 to Changfu Plaza Company via Guangdong Development Bank, Dongguan Branch on June 27, 2003, with the transfer slip indicating the type of instrument as prepaid construction approval fee.

Upon Changfu Plaza Company's application, the court of first instance obtained the following evidence from the Dongguan City Construction Bureau: temporary certificates for construction enterprise project managers, single project filing confirmation letters, filing forms for single projects by foreign enterprises, registration forms for foreign enterprises undertaking projects in Dongguan; and a set of design drawings for the project involved, obtained from the Urban and Rural Construction Planning Office of the People's Government of Dalang Town, Dongguan City. Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company did not confirm the evidence obtained from the Dongguan City Construction Bureau. All parties confirmed the drawings obtained from the Urban and Rural Construction Planning Office of the People's Government of Dalang Town.

Since the parties could not agree on the amount of the project cost in the first instance litigation, Mo Zhihua applied for the court of first instance to entrust a qualified settlement institution to settle the cost of the work performed by him. The court of first instance, upon the party's application, entrusted Dongguan Huacheng Engineering Cost Consulting Co., Ltd. to settle the cost of the work performed by Mo Zhihua. In accordance with the court's requirements, Dongguan Huacheng Engineering Cost Consulting Co., Ltd. issued two engineering cost appraisal reports: one calculated according to the pricing method, lump sum price, and adjustment margin agreed in the contract: the total project cost including tax was RMB 52,989,157.84 (including increased, decreased, and unfinished work). The other calculated based on the actual completed quantities of work and construction project categories, with reference to quotas and material price differences (not taking into account the 16.5% reduction agreed in the contract): the total cost including tax was RMB 69,066,293.11, of which profit was RMB 1,518,306.67 and tax was RMB 2,228,340.07.

After the engineering cost appraisal was issued, the court of first instance held a trial for cross-examination. The parties had no objections to the quantity of work determined by the appraisal institution. The main objections of the parties were as follows: Mo Zhihua did not cross-examine the appraisal report on the engineering cost calculated according to the contract. Regarding the appraisal report on the engineering cost calculated according to actual quantities, Mo Zhihua's opinions were: (1) He had no objection to the building area and quantity of work determined in the engineering cost appraisal. (2) For raw materials designated by Changfu Plaza Company, the cost price at the time (procurement cost + transportation cost) should be used; for raw materials not designated, the market price or the information price published by the Dongguan Construction Bureau should be uniformly applied. Specifically: 1. For river sand designated by Changfu Plaza Company from Qishi Sand Yard, it should be priced at the market price of RMB 56.67 per cubic meter at that time; for crushed stone designated by Changfu Plaza Company from Zhangmutou Railway Stone Yard and Dalingshan Railway Stone Yard, it should be priced at the market price of RMB 71.67 per cubic meter at that time; the total underpayment for these two items was RMB 1,220,933.10. 2. For all exterior wall decorative materials such as cultural bricks and mosaic tiles designated by Changfu Plaza Company to be custom-made products from Dongguan Weimei Ceramics Factory, the price of the above decorative materials should be calculated based on the factory's quoted price at that time. The cultural bricks should be calculated at RMB 130 per square meter, and the mosaic tiles at RMB 60 per square meter, resulting in a total underpayment of RMB 1,955,805.44 for these two items. 3. The anti-seepage expansion concrete for the project used UBA low-alkali high-efficiency expansion agent. The unit price of UBA expansion agent in 2003 and 2004 was RMB 1,650 per ton based on market prices, not RMB 900 per ton. Therefore, the price difference for C30 and C25 expansion concrete should be supplemented by RMB 370,499.22. 4. In 2004, the market price of finished exhaust pipes (TGWE9 type) and smoke exhaust pipes (TGCA6 type) in Dongguan was RMB 80 per meter, not RMB 65 per meter for exhaust pipes and RMB 33 per meter for smoke exhaust pipes. The price difference should be supplemented by RMB 67,605.8. 5. The fees listed in items 2 and 3 of the independent expense schedule (I) for Building C and the fees listed in independent expense schedule (II), totaling RMB 150,620, were not confirmed by both parties. They should be listed as separate items for disputed works and should not be directly settled as confirmed fees. This amount should be deducted from the total. 6. For the additional works confirmed by both parties, settlement should be calculated as separate items based on the prices already confirmed by both parties, without the need to follow the quota. The confirmed price by both parties was RMB 1,385,456.31, and the supplementary project payment should be RMB 640,000. 7. Administrative and institutional fees should be added. These fees had been collected by relevant departments totaling RMB 531,696, so this amount should be reimbursed. In addition, social security funds of RMB 66,837,953.10 x 2.9% = RMB 1,938,300.64 should be reimbursed. 8. Omitted fees totaling RMB 350,000, including: filling 4,500 cubic meters of crushed stone at the construction site for "three connections and one leveling," costing RMB 49,500; secondary material transportation costs of RMB 239,300; material storage fees for nine months of RMB 61,200. 9. The profit of RMB 1,518,306.67 determined in the appraisal report on the engineering cost calculated according to actual quantities was unfounded.

Dongshen Company argued that the contract signed by both parties was invalid due to the involvement of affiliation, so the appraisal report on the engineering cost calculated according to the contract lacked legality. Regarding the appraisal report on the engineering cost calculated according to actual quantities, Dongshen Company basically agreed with Mo Zhihua's opinions.

Changfu Plaza Company basically had no objection to the appraisal of the involved engineering quantities but argued that the foundation pit support part belonged to construction measures and was not an increase in quantity.

Dongguan Huacheng Engineering Cost Consulting Co., Ltd. responded as follows: 1. Regarding the sand and stone mentioned by Mo Zhihua, since there was no specific brand, the calculation was based on the information price published by the Construction Committee. 2. The exterior wall tiles were priced based on inquiries to Weimei Company, not the market price. 3. Since neither party designated a brand for the expansion concrete, the average price of RMB 1,200 per ton was used based on the market price at that time and information found online. 4. Since no brand was designated for the exhaust pipes and smoke exhaust pipes, the calculation was based on the information price published by the Construction Committee. If Mo Zhihua could provide purchase receipts, the court could recognize these receipts and price accordingly. 5. The deduction of RMB 100,000 from the independent expense for Building C was because Building C was not completed before the party withdrew, and site cleaning required costs, which were determined at discretion. 6. Regarding the administrative and institutional fees raised by Mo Zhihua, these were calculated as costs. Since Mo Zhihua did not submit these receipts, the cost appraisal did not include this part. 7. The omitted fees mentioned by Mo Zhihua were included in the lump sum fee. 8. Regarding the additional works issue, some parts were negotiated by both parties. In the appraisal report on the engineering cost calculated according to the contract, pricing was based on the agreement between the parties; in the appraisal report on the engineering cost calculated according to actual quantities, pricing was based on the actual quantity of work completed. 9. Regarding the foundation pit support issue raised by Changfu Plaza Company, the cost for this part had been listed separately, and it was up to the court to determine whether to include it in the total engineering cost.

The court of first instance held that, considering the case facts and the matters to be adjudicated, the focus issues were as follows: First, the validity of the contract in this case; Second, how to determine the project cost in this case; Third, whether Changfu Plaza Company's counterclaim should be supported; Fourth, whether the performance bond of RMB 2.7 million paid by Mo Zhihua should be returned by Changfu Plaza Company; Fifth, whether Dongshen Company's claims should be supported.

I. Regarding the validity of the contract in this case. In this case, Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company admitted during the trial of first instance and in the proceedings that Mo Zhihua was affiliated with Dongshen Company to undertake the involved project. According to Article 12 of the *Construction Law of the People's Republic of China*: "Construction enterprises, survey units, design units, and project supervision units engaged in construction activities shall meet the following conditions: (1) Have a registered capital that complies with national regulations; (2) Have professional and technical personnel with statutory qualifications appropriate to their construction activities; (3) Have the technical equipment necessary for engaging in relevant construction activities; (4) Other conditions stipulated by laws and administrative regulations." And Article 26: "Units undertaking construction projects shall hold qualification certificates obtained in accordance with the law and undertake projects within the business scope permitted by their qualification level. Construction enterprises are prohibited from undertaking projects beyond the business scope permitted by their qualification level, or from undertaking projects in the name of other construction enterprises in any form. Construction enterprises are prohibited from allowing other units or individuals to use their qualification certificates or business licenses to undertake projects in the name of the enterprise in any form." Mo Zhihua, as a natural person, did not have the qualification to undertake construction projects. Mo Zhihua's affiliation with a qualified construction enterprise, Dongshen Company, to undertake the project violated the mandatory provisions of the above laws. According to Article 52 of the *Contract Law of the People's Republic of China*: "... A contract is invalid under any of the following circumstances: ... (5) Violating mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations." And Article 1 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Construction Project Contracts*: "If a construction project contract falls under any of the following circumstances, it shall be deemed invalid according to Article 52(5) of the *Contract Law*: (2) An actual builder without qualifications borrows the name of a qualified construction enterprise." The *Preliminary Agreement on Changfu Plaza Project*, the *Dongguan Construction Project Construction Contract*, and the *Dalang Changfu Commercial Plaza Construction Project Construction Contract* signed between Dongshen Company and Changfu Plaza Company should be determined as invalid according to law. According to the *Cooperation Agreement on Changfu Commercial Plaza Project* signed between the two plaintiffs, which stipulated: "Both Party A and Party B must ensure that the contents of this agreement are not disclosed externally and are kept strictly confidential...", combined with the facts that in the *Preliminary Agreement on Changfu Plaza Project*, Party B was listed as Dongshen Company; in the *Dalang Changfu Commercial Plaza Construction Project Construction Contract*, the contractor was listed as Dongshen Company; in the *Dongguan Construction Project Construction Contract*, the contractor was listed as Dongshen Company; the construction unit on relevant site visit certificates and the addressee on project contact forms were all signed as Dongshen Company; the addressee on relevant correspondence regarding project costs was listed as the Project Manager Department of Shenzhen Dongshen Engineering Co., Ltd., Dalang Changfu Commercial Plaza; in the acceptance records for main structure sub-division works, the seal for the construction unit was Dongshen Company; the construction unit indicated in hidden work records was Dongshen Company; the transfer unit on project handover forms was Dongshen Company and the Project Manager Department of Shenzhen Dongshen Engineering Co., Ltd., Dalang Changfu Commercial Plaza; the receipts submitted by Changfu Plaza Company showed that progress payments for the involved project were paid to Dongshen Company; in relevant coordination meetings, Mo Zhihua participated in the capacity of a staff member of the "construction unit Shenzhen Dongshen Engineering Co., Ltd."; even the loan notes and IOUs submitted by Mo Zhihua were all made in the name of the Project Manager Department of Dongshen Company, Dalang Changfu Commercial Plaza. The above evidence and facts indicate that in the signing and performance of the contract, the legal relationship with Changfu Plaza Company was with Dongshen Company. At the same time, Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company failed to provide sufficient evidence to prove that Changfu Plaza Company was aware of the affiliation relationship between Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company. Therefore, the fundamental reason for the invalidity of the contract in this case was Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company. Dongshen Company, knowing that Mo Zhihua had no construction qualification, still allowed him to undertake the project through affiliation, which was illegal, and thus should bear full fault liability.

II. Regarding how to determine the project cost in this case. Article 58 of the *Contract Law of the People's Republic of China* stipulates: "After a contract is confirmed as invalid or rescinded, any property acquired as a result of the contract shall be returned; if return is impossible or unnecessary, compensation shall be made at a discounted price. The party at fault shall compensate the other party for the losses suffered as a result; if both parties are at fault, they shall bear their respective liabilities." In this case, Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company requested Changfu Plaza Company to pay the project cost, while Changfu Plaza Company obtained the buildings in which Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company had materialized their labor and construction materials. Given the particularity of construction project contracts, although the contract was confirmed invalid, the performed contents could not be restored to the pre-contract state through return, so the only option was to handle it by way of compensation at a discounted price. However, the parties failed to reach an agreement on how to implement this. As mentioned above, the reason for the invalidity of the contract in this case was Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company. Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company should not, due to their fault leading to the contract's invalidity, obtain more benefits than if the valid contract had been performed on schedule. At the same time, given that Changfu Plaza Company did not raise objections to the quality of the completed works, although the contract in this case was invalid, the project cost should still be calculated based on the actual quantity of work completed and the settlement method agreed in the contract. The cost of increases, decreases, or changes should be calculated with reference to the contract terms and the usual practices of the appraisal unit. The court of first instance could only determine the cost by referencing the contract and expert appraisal conclusions.

There were two contracts in this case: the *Dongguan Construction Project Construction Contract* (hereinafter referred to as the "Recorded Contract") dated May 19, 2003, used for filing, and the *Dalang Changfu Commercial Plaza Construction Project Construction Contract* dated May 21, 2003. Which contract should be used as the basis for settlement? Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company argued that the contract dated May 21, 2003, should prevail. Changfu Plaza Company stated that if a judgment was to be made, the Recorded Contract should prevail; if mediation was to be conducted, the contract dated May 21, 2003, could be used. However, Changfu Plaza Company did not object to the fact that the appraisal institution, in the appraisal report on the engineering cost calculated according to the contract, had determined the contract dated May 21, 2003, as the basis for settlement. It could be determined that the contract dated May 21, 2003, reflected the true intentions of the parties. Therefore, the contract dated May 21, 2003, should be used as the basis for settlement in this case (hereinafter referred to as the "Contract").

The court of first instance commissioned Dongguan Huacheng Engineering Cost Consulting Co., Ltd. to appraise the project cost. The conclusion was: the engineering cost calculated according to the contract was RMB 52,989,157.84. Since the contract stipulated that all taxes payable on the project cost, including business tax, education surcharge, urban maintenance and construction tax, and withholding income tax, should be paid by the contractor to the tax authority, and all other costs outside the budget, such as equipment and personnel mobilization and demobilization fees, protective net fees, sanitation fees, earth borrowing resource fees, earth disposal fees, and construction interference between adjacent contractors, had been comprehensively considered by the contractor in the bid quotation and reflected in the cost decline rate, and should not be calculated during settlement. Therefore, the relevant administrative and institutional fees were already included in the contract price. Mo Zhihua's request to add administrative and institutional fees of RMB 531,696 was not supported. Since Mo Zhihua failed to provide evidence, the court of first instance did not support his request to add social security funds of RMB 1,938,300.64. Regarding Changfu Plaza Company's argument that the foundation pit support was not a physical project but a construction measure, after consulting the appraisal institution, the foundation pit support was considered a physical project. Therefore, the foundation pit support should be treated as additional works, and its cost should be included in the project cost. Regarding Mo Zhihua's objection that the appraisal institution calculated some materials based on market inquiry prices, and his request to use the sum of his purchase price and transportation cost as the material price, since the contract had fixed the origin and specifications of the above materials, and the contract in Article 2.7 "Determination of Material Prices" stipulated: "The materials in this project shall be calculated according to the prices of the materials listed in Article 2.6 of this contract, and no adjustment shall be made during settlement," this meant that at the time of contract signing, the contract price had already stipulated the method for pricing during settlement. Therefore, Mo Zhihua's request to increase the price of river sand and crushed stone was not supported by the court of first instance. Since the appraisers of the appraisal unit were professionals with specialized knowledge and the appraisal procedure was lawful, it was appropriate for the appraisal institution to calculate the prices of materials not covered by the quota based on market inquiry prices. The court of first instance did not support Mo Zhihua's request to increase the price differences for cultural bricks, mosaic tiles, exhaust pipes, smoke exhaust pipes, and C30 and C25 expansion concrete. Regarding the issue of reduced works in the independent expense schedule for Building C raised by Mo Zhihua, the settlement calculated according to the contract included a fee of RMB 100,000 for clearing and transporting garbage. Since the contract dated May 21, 2003, stipulated that the budget lump sum fee included garbage transportation after completion and clearing, the appraisal institution's deduction of this fee complied with the contract. As for the deduction of 12,030 holes for repairing openings and the deduction of 10 cubic meters of concrete in the independent expense schedule for Building C, this quantity was based on the *Actual Quantities of Uncompleted Works of Changfu Plaza* jointly confirmed by Dongshen Company, Changfu Plaza Company, and the supervision company Dongguan Yuejian Supervision Engineering Co., Ltd. with seals. As uncompleted works, these fees should be deducted when calculating the project cost. Mo Zhihua's claim to include the fees involved in the independent expense schedule for Building C lacked basis and was not supported by the court of first instance. Regarding Mo Zhihua's request to add on-site visa fees of RMB 350,000, Mo Zhihua submitted on-site visa certificates dated September 17, 2003, and October 30, 2004, as evidence. Given that in the column for "Dongguan Yuejian Supervision Engineering Co., Ltd." on the visa certificates, although there was an engineer's signature, the company's seal was not affixed, and Changfu Plaza Company did not confirm it. Mo Zhihua failed to provide evidence to prove that the engineer who signed was an on-site supervisor of Dongguan Yuejian Supervision Engineering Co., Ltd. Therefore, Mo Zhihua's evidence could not prove that this fee had been incurred by him and approved by Changfu Plaza Company. Mo Zhihua's request was rejected. Upon inquiry with Dongguan Huacheng Engineering Cost Consulting Co., Ltd., Mo Zhihua's other opinions regarding the appraisal report on the engineering cost calculated according to actual quantities had no impact on the engineering cost calculated according to the contract. In summary, the total project cost was RMB 52,989,157.84.

III. Whether the requests of Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company for payment of project cost should be supported. The *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Construction Project Contracts* stipulates that the precondition for payment of project cost is that the project has passed the final acceptance inspection and is qualified. As a public product, the quality of the involved project could not be determined solely by the parties' confirmation; it needed to be verified through a legal acceptance inspection by the construction administrative authority. Since Mo Zhihua refused to provide construction materials, the involved project could not enter the final acceptance procedure. At the same time, Mo Zhihua, by requesting payment of project cost, bore the burden of proving that the project he had constructed had passed the final acceptance inspection and was qualified. Now that Mo Zhihua did not cooperate with the final acceptance, his claim for payment of project cost was rejected according to law.

IV. Whether the performance bond of RMB 2.7 million paid by Mo Zhihua should be returned by Changfu Plaza Company. Mo Zhihua submitted a bank transfer slip from China Construction Bank dated April 30, 2003, a bank transfer slip from Guangdong Development Bank Dongguan Branch dated May 23, 2003, a certificate from Qingyuan Qingxin Construction and Installation Engineering Company Dongguan Branch, and a certificate from Dongguan Jinxinlian Industrial Investment Co., Ltd., to prove that he had paid a performance bond of RMB 2.7 million. Changfu Plaza Company had no objection to the authenticity of the two bank transfer slips and confirmed receipt of the above performance bond. However, it did not confirm the authenticity of the certificates from Qingyuan Qingxin Construction and Installation Engineering Company Dongguan Branch and Dongguan Jinxinlian Industrial Investment Co., Ltd., arguing that the above certificates could not prove that the performance bond belonged to Mo Zhihua. However, Dongshen Company confirmed that the performance bond of RMB 2.7 million belonged to Mo Zhihua and was paid by him. Since Changfu Plaza Company confirmed that it had received the performance bond stipulated in the contract, and at the time of signing the contract, the other party was Dongshen Company, and now Dongshen Company admitted that the above performance bond belonged to Mo Zhihua, it should be confirmed that the performance bond of RMB 2.7 million received by Changfu Plaza Company belonged to Mo Zhihua. Since the contract was invalid, Changfu Plaza Company should return the performance bond obtained under the contract to Mo Zhihua. The court of first instance supported Mo Zhihua's request for Changfu Plaza Company to return the performance bond of RMB 2.7 million. Regarding the interest on the performance bond, since the contract did not provide for it, Changfu Plaza Company should start paying interest from the date of Mo Zhihua's request, i.e., the date Mo Zhihua filed the lawsuit, at the same period loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China.

V. Whether Dongshen Company's claims should be supported. Regarding Dongshen Company's request for Changfu Plaza Company to pay project cost and its interest, and to return the performance bond of RMB 2.7 million and its interest, since Dongshen Company's act of lending its qualification to Mo Zhihua to undertake the involved project also violated national prohibitive provisions and was an invalid civil act. At the same time, Dongshen Company did not actually undertake the involved project, and the performance bond was actually paid by Mo Zhihua. Therefore, Dongshen Company's claims were not supported by the court of first instance.

6. Whether Changfu Plaza Company's counterclaim should be upheld. Changfu Plaza Company had already paid RMB 57,860,815.68 in project funds, and Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company should return the overpaid project funds of RMB 4,871,657.84 to Changfu Plaza Company. Although the contract was invalid, Changfu Plaza Company had actually advanced the aforesaid project funds, and Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company had actually occupied the funds. Based on the principle of fairness, Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company should pay interest on the advanced project funds to Changfu Plaza Company. Changfu Plaza Company requested Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company to return the interest on the overpaid project funds, with the commencement date being the day after the contractual completion date, i.e., August 1, 2004. Since the project in question was not completed at the time Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company filed the lawsuit and the contract was invalid, the aforesaid interest should be calculated from the date of the lawsuit, i.e., April 20, 2005. That is, Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company should pay interest on the overpaid project funds to Changfu Plaza Company at the same-period loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China from April 20, 2005, until the date of full payment. Changfu Plaza Company counterclaimed for liquidated damages for delay in completion due to Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company. Since the contract was invalid, there was no issue of breach of contract; therefore, the court of first instance did not uphold this counterclaim. Changfu Plaza Company provided lease contracts to prove its rental losses due to Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company's failure to complete on time, but the aforesaid contracts failed to indicate that the reduction in rent for certain lessees and the failure to sign lease contracts with certain lessees were caused by Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company's failure to complete on time. Therefore, the court of first instance did not uphold this counterclaim. As for the other economic losses claimed by Changfu Plaza Company, since no evidence was provided, the court of first instance also did not uphold this counterclaim.

In summary, in accordance with Article 52(5) and Article 58 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 12 and 26 of the Construction Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 1, 2, 71, and 72 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Litigation, and Article 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases Involving Disputes over Construction Project Construction Contracts, the court of first instance rendered judgment on November 30, 2007, as follows: 1. The "Preliminary Agreement for the Changfu Plaza Project," the "Dongguan Construction Project Construction Contract," and the "Dalang Changfu Commercial Plaza Construction Project Construction Contract" signed between Dongshen Company and Changfu Plaza Company are invalid. 2. Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company shall, within ten days from the date this judgment becomes legally effective, return the overpaid project funds of RMB 4,871,657.84 and interest thereon (calculated from April 20, 2005, at the same-period loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China until the date of full payment) to Changfu Plaza Company. 3. Changfu Plaza Company shall, within ten days from the date this judgment becomes legally effective, return the performance bond of RMB 2,700,000 paid by Mo Zhihua and interest thereon (calculated from April 20, 2005, at the same-period loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China until the date of full payment) to Mo Zhihua. 4. Mo Zhihua's other claims are dismissed. 5. Dongshen Company's claims are dismissed. 6. The other counterclaims of Changfu Plaza Company are dismissed. If any party fails to perform the monetary obligation within the period specified in this judgment, it shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, pay double the interest on the debt during the period of delayed performance. The litigation costs for the main action of RMB 137,059, the preservation fee of RMB 75,520, and the appraisal and settlement fee of RMB 611,146, totaling RMB 823,725, shall be borne by Mo Zhihua in the amount of RMB 358,320, by Dongshen Company in the amount of RMB 358,320, and by Changfu Plaza Company in the amount of RMB 107,085. The litigation costs for the counterclaim of RMB 44,360 shall be borne by Changfu Plaza Company (the counterclaim plaintiff) in the amount of RMB 16,618, by Mo Zhihua in the amount of RMB 13,871, and by Dongshen Company in the amount of RMB 13,871.

Mo Zhihua, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the Guangdong High People's Court, arguing: (1) The construction contract signed by the parties is invalid and should be settled based on actual amounts. The "Dalang Changfu Commercial Plaza Construction Project Construction Contract" signed on May 21, 2003, was the basis for actual construction, but not for settlement. (2) The Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases Involving Disputes over Construction Project Construction Contracts does not stipulate that no project payment can be made for projects that have not passed acceptance inspection. All individual sub-projects of the project in question have passed acceptance inspection, only comprehensive acceptance inspection has not been conducted, and Changfu Plaza Company has already used the construction project. (3) The judgment of first instance violates the principle of fairness. The contract between the parties is invalid. Changfu Plaza Company had always negotiated the contract with Mo Zhihua personally, the performance bond was paid by Mo Zhihua, the construction management was handled by Mo Zhihua, and Changfu Plaza also paid project funds to Mo Zhihua. These facts sufficiently prove that Changfu Plaza Company had always known and recognized Mo Zhihua as the actual constructor. The judgment of first instance improperly attributed all fault liability for the invalidity of the contract to Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company. (4) The court of first instance improperly extended the trial period, harming the interests of the parties. Therefore, Mo Zhihua requested the reversal of the judgment of first instance and the upholding of his claims.

Dongshen Company, also dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed, arguing: (1) Changfu Plaza Company was aware of Mo Zhihua's illegal affiliation for construction. The judgment of first instance wrongly attributed all fault liability to Dongshen Company and Mo Zhihua. At the time of signing the contract, Changfu Plaza Company designated Mo Zhihua as the project manager of the constructor, and Mo Zhihua's "Project Manager Certificate" attached to the contract also showed that he was not an employee of Changfu Plaza Company. Moreover, during the construction period, Changfu Plaza Company remitted over RMB 40 million in project funds to Mo Zhihua's designated account, all of which indicated that the illegal affiliation was actively facilitated by Changfu Plaza Company. (2) The judgment of first instance erred in ascertaining the project cost. The contract is invalid, yet the court of first instance proceeded with settlement based on the invalid contract, which is logically contradictory. When preparing the construction budget quotation, the drawings were not yet finalized, there were serious omissions, and the unit construction price was significantly lower than the construction cost. Settlement based on the invalid contract is manifestly unfair. (3) The Changfu Commercial Plaza project has actually been delivered for use and has been almost fully sold. According to the contract, it should be deemed as having passed acceptance inspection. (4) The judgment of first instance ordering Dongshen Company and Mo Zhihua to jointly satisfy Changfu Plaza Company's RMB 4.87 million project fund claim is not in accordance with the law. The affiliated person's assets should first be used to satisfy the debt, and the affiliated entity should bear supplementary liability. Therefore, Dongshen Company requested: the reversal of items 2, 3, and 5 of the judgment of first instance, and a judgment in favor of Dongshen Company's claims.

In response to Mo Zhihua's appeal, Changfu Plaza Company argued that: (1) In accordance with Article 21 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases Involving Disputes over Construction Project Construction Contracts, the filed construction contract should be used as the basis for audit and settlement in this case. (2) The court of first instance had substantively addressed the issue of settlement of project funds between the parties, and there was no factual basis for the claim that the court of first instance had substantively rejected Mo Zhihua's request for payment of project funds. (3) In the negotiation, formal contract signing, project quality acceptance, payment of project funds, project demobilization, handling of project tail-end matters, project dispute negotiations, and negotiations with the Dongguan Construction Bureau, all were handled by Dongshen Company issuing letters of introduction, signing the relevant contracts, providing bank account numbers for receipt, issuing receipts, and organizing personnel. The illegal affiliation contract signed between Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company was a secret agreement, with a penalty of RMB 100,000 for disclosure. These facts prove that all fault for the illegal affiliation should be borne by Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company. (4) Due to Mo Zhihua's illegal affiliation and disruption of the construction market, the property in question has still not been able to complete the record-filing process, creating a significant social hazard. Changfu Plaza Company requested the court of second instance to uphold its legitimate rights and interests.

In response to Dongshen Company's appeal, Changfu Plaza Company argued that Dongshen Company's inference that Changfu Plaza Company should have known of the illegal affiliation lacked factual basis. The court of first instance's determination of the project cost and its handling method were fundamentally fair and lawful. The judgment of first instance that Dongshen Company bore joint liability for the return of project funds was reasonable and lawful. Changfu Plaza Company requested the court of second instance to uphold its interests.

The facts found by the court of second instance were the same as those found by the court of first instance.

The court of second instance held that the contracts signed by Mo Zhihua in the name of Dongshen Company with Changfu Plaza Company, including the "Dalang Changfu Commercial Plaza Construction Project Construction Contract," violated Article 26(2) of the Construction Law of the People's Republic of China and should be confirmed as invalid. Given the special nature of construction project contracts, the parties could not mutually return performance, so the matter could only be handled by way of compensation at a discounted value. From the existing evidence, there was no evidence showing that Changfu Plaza Company knew of Mo Zhihua's affiliation with Dongshen Company for construction at the time of signing or performance. Therefore, the fault for the invalidity of the contract should be borne by Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company.

Regarding Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company's argument that the contract was invalid, that Changfu Plaza Company was aware of the affiliation and thus also at fault, and that the completed project should be settled based on actual amounts: Whether during the signing or performance of the contract, Mo Zhihua appeared in the capacity of project manager of Dongshen Company, and Mo Zhihua's actions represented Dongshen Company. The fact that Changfu Plaza Company negotiated project matters with Mo Zhihua and paid project funds based on Mo Zhihua's instructions could not prove that Changfu Plaza Company knew of the affiliation between Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company. The evidence submitted by Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company that Changfu Plaza Company knew of their affiliation was insufficient and was not accepted. In this case, the court of first instance entrusted an intermediary agency to calculate the completed project costs based on the contract and based on actual amounts. The project cost based on actual amounts was significantly higher than the project cost based on the contract price. Since Changfu Plaza Company was not at fault and the disputed project had been actually used, in accordance with the principles of fairness and good faith, the case could not impose losses beyond the contract on Changfu Plaza Company, the party without fault. Moreover, by analogy with Article 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases Involving Disputes over Construction Project Construction Contracts, the following conclusion could be drawn: Unless the reason for the invalidity of the contract lies in the price terms violating mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, an invalid construction contract should still determine the project cost in accordance with the contract terms. Therefore, the court of first instance's decision to determine the cost of the completed project by reference to the original contract terms was correct and was upheld. Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company's basis for claiming settlement based on actual amounts was insufficient and was not supported. Since the settlement was based on the contract terms, Changfu Plaza Company had already overpaid the project funds. Therefore, Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company's request for Changfu Plaza to continue paying project funds lacked basis and was also not supported.

Regarding Dongshen Company's argument that Mo Zhihua had affiliated with it for operations, and therefore the overpaid project funds should be repaid from Mo Zhihua's assets, with Dongshen Company only bearing supplementary liability rather than joint liability: Mo Zhihua signed the contract with Changfu Plaza Company in the name of Dongshen Company, carried out the construction, and received project funds, and Dongshen Company had acknowledged this. Therefore, the project funds paid by Changfu Plaza Company should be deemed to have been jointly received by Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company, and they should jointly bear the repayment obligation. Dongshen Company's grounds for this appeal were insufficient and were not supported. In summary, the judgment of first instance had clear findings of fact, correct application of law, and should be upheld in accordance with the law. In accordance with Article 153(1)(a) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court of second instance rendered judgment: The appeal was dismissed and the original judgment was affirmed. The litigation costs for the appeal of RMB 181,419 were borne equally by Dongshen Company and Mo Zhihua, each paying RMB 90,709.50.

Mo Zhihua, dissatisfied with this judgment, applied to this Court for retrial, arguing: (1) Dongguan Huacheng Engineering Cost Consulting Co., Ltd. had produced two appraisal conclusions based on the contract terms and actual settlement, respectively: the "Engineering Cost Appraisal Report" with a total cost including tax of RMB 52,989,157.84 (referred to as the contract cost appraisal report) and the "Engineering Cost Appraisal Report" with a total cost including tax of RMB 69,066,293.11. The judgment of the original trial determined the project cost based on the "Contract Cost Appraisal Report," which had not been subject to cross-examination by Mo Zhihua. Pursuant to Article 179(1)(4) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, if the main evidence relied upon by the court has not been cross-examined, a retrial should be granted. (2) The "Contract Cost Appraisal Report" contained the following errors: 1. On February 28, 2004, the parties signed a "Meeting Minutes," which clarified that they had reached an agreement to each bear 50% of the price difference for the two main materials, steel and cement. However, the appraisal report failed to deduct the price difference for steel and cement in accordance with this agreement, omitting appraisal materials. 2. The "Engineering Cost Appraisal Report" contained instances of undercounting and omission for the increased works and overcounting for the reduced works. Specific reasons were set out in the attachment "Objections to the Contract Settlement Section of the 'Engineering Cost Appraisal Report' for the Dalang Changfu Plaza Project." 3. According to Article 48 of the Construction Law of the People's Republic of China, construction enterprises must take out accidental injury insurance for workers engaged in dangerous operations and pay the insurance premiums. Mo Zhihua legally paid social security premiums of RMB 198,300.64, which proved that Mo Zhihua was a law-abiding citizen who legally fulfilled the mandatory insurance obligations under the Construction Law. The court of first instance failed to verify this and simply rejected the claim on the grounds of no evidence, which was contrary to the facts. (3) The settlement clause in the "Dalang Changfu Commercial Plaza Construction Project Construction Contract" dated May 21, 2003, was a conditional clause. In the "Preliminary Agreement for the Changfu Plaza Project" dated May 11, 2003, Changfu Plaza Company promised to contract the electrical installation works, streetscape works, and secondary decoration works to Mo Zhihua, on the condition that the total project cost could be reduced by 16.5%. However, Changfu Plaza Company did not fulfill this, thereby depriving the settlement clause of the May 21, 2003 contract of the conditions and basis for its application. The project in dispute had not undergone completion acceptance and was an unfinished project. The project involved increased works and design changes. Mo Zhihua claimed project funds from Changfu Plaza Company based on the actual completed quantities, and the company also paid based on actual quantities, not in accordance with the contract. The original judgment's reliance on the "Dalang Changfu Commercial Plaza Construction Project Construction Contract" dated May 21, 2003, for settlement of project funds was erroneous. (4) Changfu Plaza Company was aware that Mo Zhihua had affiliated with Dongshen Company to contract this project. The court of first instance incorrectly found that Changfu Plaza Company was unaware, and attributed all fault for the invalidity of the contract to Mo Zhihua. Pursuant to Article 179(1)(2), (4), and (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Mo Zhihua applied for a retrial.

Changfu Plaza Company responded, arguing that the original judgment had clear findings of fact and correct application of law and should be upheld.

Upon retrial, this Court found: Regarding the issue of material price differences, mediation was conducted under the auspices of the Dongguan Construction Bureau of Guangdong Province. Chen Zhipeng, as the representative of Changfu Plaza Company, stated at the Dalang Changfu Plaza project meeting that Changfu Plaza Company was willing to bear 50% of the price difference for the two main materials, approximately RMB 3.8 million, and, as a gesture of sincerity, was willing to compensate Dongshen Company an additional RMB 1 million, totaling approximately RMB 4.8 million.

This Court found the other facts in the retrial to be the same as those found in the first instance and second instance.

This Court held that the issues in dispute between the parties in the retrial were: 1. Whether the original judgment's determination of liability for the invalidity of the contract was appropriate. 2. How the project funds for the project in question should be calculated. This includes: (a) Whether the project funds should be settled in accordance with the contract terms or based on actual amounts; (b) Whether the "Contract Cost Appraisal Report" relied upon by the court of first instance had been subject to cross-examination; (c) Whether the appraisal report was erroneous in determining the amount of project funds.

1. Whether the original judgment's determination of liability for the invalidity of the contract was appropriate.

Neither party disputed the invalidity of the contract, but Mo Zhihua argued that the original judgment's determination of liability for the invalidity was unjust. Mo Zhihua claimed that Changfu Plaza Company should have been aware of his affiliation with Dongshen Company but failed to provide corresponding evidence to support his claim. From the content of the confidentiality agreement signed between Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company, it was difficult for third parties outside the confidentiality agreement to know of their affiliation. The contracting parties in the dispute were Changfu Plaza Company and Dongshen Company. The receipts submitted by Changfu Plaza Company showed that progress payments for the project were made to Dongshen Company, and Mo Zhihua participated in coordination meetings as a staff member of Dongshen Company. The IOUs and loan receipts submitted by Mo Zhihua were also made in the name of the Project Manager Department of Dongshen Company's Dalang Changfu Commercial Plaza. The above evidence and facts indicated that the legal relationship in the signing and performance of the contract was with Dongshen Company, not Mo Zhihua. Therefore, Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company should bear all liability for the invalidity of the contract. The original judgment's determination of liability for the invalidity of the contract was not improper. Even if Changfu Plaza Company had knowledge and bore some fault, it would not affect the substantive outcome of the case. Allocation of fault is only relevant in calculating damages, and does not affect the determination of the amount of project funds. Pursuant to Article 58 of the Contract Law, "If a contract is invalid or rescinded, any property obtained under the contract shall be returned. If it cannot be returned or return is unnecessary, compensation shall be made at a discounted value. The party at fault shall compensate the other party for losses incurred thereby. If both parties are at fault, each shall bear corresponding liability." In this case, the parties only disputed the amount of project funds to be calculated. Neither party filed a claim for damages. Therefore, the determination of fault liability did not affect the calculation of the amount of project funds.

2. How the project funds for the project in question should be calculated.

(a) Regarding the basis for calculating the project funds. The issue was whether the project funds should be settled in accordance with the contract terms or based on actual amounts. Given the special nature of construction projects, although the contract was invalid, the labor and building materials of Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company had been incorporated into the project in question. Pursuant to Article 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases Involving Disputes over Construction Project Construction Contracts, an invalid construction contract should be handled by reference to the valid contract, and the project funds should be calculated by reference to the contract terms. Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company's claim that the project funds should be settled based on actual amounts lacked basis. Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company should not obtain greater benefits than they would have if the contract were valid. The project funds for the project in question should be settled in accordance with the contract terms.

(2) Whether the Contract Cost Appraisal Report was subject to cross-examination. Mo Zhihua claimed that the Contract Cost Appraisal Report was not cross-examined by him. On September 6, 2006, the court of first instance held a hearing in this case, with Mo Zhihua, Changfu Plaza Company, Dongshen Company, and the appraisal institution all participating in the hearing. During the hearing of the first instance, the court of first instance requested all parties to present their opinions on the two appraisal reports in this case. Mo Zhihua gave his opinion on the appraisal report based on actual settlement, but did not recognize the appraisal report based on contract settlement, and therefore did not cross-examine it. The court of first instance had presented the relevant evidentiary materials in court and required the parties to cross-examine each other. Mo Zhihua's claim that the Contract Cost Appraisal Report was not cross-examined is inconsistent with the facts.

(3) Whether there is an error in the calculation of the amount of project funds involved in the appraisal report. Mo Zhihua claimed that the appraisal report had undercounted and omitted certain portions of the additional works, and had overcounted the reduced works. Dongguan Huacheng Engineering Cost Consulting Co., Ltd. has already responded to his objections. The appraisal institution is qualified and the appraisal procedure is lawful. Therefore, Mo Zhihua's claim that the appraisal amount is erroneous lacks basis, and this Court does not support it.

Regarding whether Changfu Plaza Company overpaid Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company more than 4.8 million yuan in project funds. Based on the facts ascertained by this Court upon retrial, Mo Zhihua and Changfu Plaza Company had conducted mediation under the auspices of the Dongguan Construction Bureau. With respect to the issue of the 7.6 million yuan price difference for steel and cement, Changfu Plaza Company expressed its willingness to bear 50%. On this basis, Changfu Plaza Company additionally compensated 1 million yuan, totaling approximately 4.8 million yuan. Changfu Plaza Company made this expression of intent, and at the same time, it had also already overpaid 4.8 million yuan in project funds. This act should be recognized as a voluntary compensation to Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company. Its current claim that Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company should return the overpaid project funds violates the principle of good faith, and this Court does not support it. The original judgment's determination that Mo Zhihua and Dongshen Company should return 4,871,657.84 yuan of overpaid project funds to Changfu Plaza Company plus interest on that amount was clearly improper and should be corrected. In summary, pursuant to Article 186, Paragraph 1, and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Set aside the Civil Judgment (2008) Yue Gao Fa Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 71 of the Guangdong High People's Court;

2. Affirm Items 1, 3, 4, 5, and 6 of the Civil Judgment (2005) Dong Zhong Fa Min Yi Chu Zi No. 11 of the Dongguan Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province;

3. Set aside Item 2 of the Civil Judgment (2005) Dong Zhong Fa Min Yi Chu Zi No. 11 of the Dongguan Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province.

The litigation costs for the main action in the first instance are 137,059 yuan, the preservation costs are 75,520 yuan, and the appraisal fees are 611,146 yuan, totaling 823,725 yuan, to be borne by Mo Zhihua in the amount of 358,320 yuan, by Shenzhen Dongshen Engineering Co., Ltd. in the amount of 358,320 yuan, and by Dongguan Changfu Plaza Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. in the amount of 107,085 yuan. The litigation costs for the counterclaim are 44,360 yuan, to be borne by Dongguan Changfu Plaza Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.

The costs for the second instance are 181,419 yuan, to be borne by Mo Zhihua in the amount of 63,496.65 yuan, by Shenzhen Dongshen Engineering Co., Ltd. in the amount of 63,496.65 yuan, and by Dongguan Changfu Plaza Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. in the amount of 54,425.70 yuan.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Zhang Jinxian

Acting Judge: Song Chunyu

Acting Judge: Wang Yuying
